# StatusPan

> StatusPan is an open-source local board for which AI agent is working on what. One Go binary listens on loopback. Agents push job updates and never get a callback. A self-hosted Cloudflare relay is optional for agents on another machine. Version 0.3.0.

The board is at http://127.0.0.1:4477 by default, or at `$STATUSPAN_ADDR` if you set one.

## Install and run

Do these steps in order. This is enough to install StatusPan, start the board, and post a first job.

1. Install the CLI (macOS or Linux):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://statuspan.com/install.sh | sh
```

The installer puts the binary in `/usr/local/bin` when you are root or that directory is writable, otherwise in `~/.local/bin`. It does not edit your shell rc files.

2. Make sure `statuspan` is on PATH:

```bash
command -v statuspan
```

If that prints nothing, add the install directory to PATH, or call the binary by the full path the installer printed:

```bash
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
command -v statuspan
# or run it by full path, for example:
#   ~/.local/bin/statuspan serve
#   /usr/local/bin/statuspan serve
```

To keep PATH for new shells, append that `export` line to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`. Do not skip this check. `statuspan: command not found` means the install directory is not on PATH.

3. Start the board in the background. It listens only on loopback. The default address is `127.0.0.1:4477`. To use another loopback port (for example if 4477 is already taken), set `STATUSPAN_ADDR`. You can also set `STATUSPAN_DATA` to a separate data directory (default `~/.config/statuspan`):

```bash
export STATUSPAN_ADDR=127.0.0.1:4477
# throwaway port example: export STATUSPAN_ADDR=127.0.0.1:14477
statuspan serve &
```

`statuspan serve --addr 127.0.0.1:14477` is the same as setting `STATUSPAN_ADDR`. Leave the process running.

4. Health-check the board. If the connection is refused, wait a second and try again until you get JSON with a `jobs` array (empty is fine):

```bash
curl -s "http://${STATUSPAN_ADDR:-127.0.0.1:4477}/api/jobs"
```

Then open the board at `http://127.0.0.1:4477`, or at whatever host:port you set in `STATUSPAN_ADDR`.

5. Post a test job. If you set `STATUSPAN_ADDR`, `statuspan post` uses it automatically. You can also pass `--addr 127.0.0.1:14477`.

```bash
statuspan post --agent "My Agent" --job hello --state running --note "first post"
```

6. Confirm it shows on the board. Reload the page, or:

```bash
curl -s "http://${STATUSPAN_ADDR:-127.0.0.1:4477}/api/jobs"
statuspan ls
```

You should see My Agent / hello as running.

7. Install the agent skill so later sessions can post without this guide:

```bash
statuspan agent install
```

8. Optional: if this machine is not the one running the board, connect it to your relay instead of posting to localhost. See [Connect another machine to your relay](#connect-another-machine-to-your-relay) below, or <https://statuspan.com/relay>.


On macOS, [StatusPan.dmg](https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest/download/StatusPan.dmg) is a WKWebView window on the local board. It starts the bundled `statuspan serve` if nothing answers on `STATUSPAN_ADDR` (default `127.0.0.1:4477`), and it stops only a daemon it started.

Post one update. The CLI posts to the relay when `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL`, `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE`, and `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE` are set, and to the local daemon otherwise.

```bash
statuspan post --agent "My Agent" --job build-1 --state running --progress 40
```

As a backup, you can always use the URL with plain curl, as long as the URL is the one where StatusPan is actually running.

```bash
curl -s -X POST "${STATUSPAN_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:4477/api/jobs}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"agent":"My Agent","job_id":"build-1","state":"running","progress":40}'
```

## Protocol

- States you can post: `queued`, `running`, `blocked`, `done`, `failed`.
- `stalled` and `abandoned` are derived when the board is read. Bots cannot post them.
- A running job with no heartbeat for `ttl` seconds (default 600) is stalled. Queued, blocked, done, and failed do not stall.
- The latest `seq` for an `(agent, job_id)` wins. An equal or older seq stays in history and does not change the job. Omit `seq` and the post applies.
- Partial updates merge. Omitted fields stay as they are. A new job needs `state`. A later post may omit it.
- Fire and forget. If StatusPan is offline, keep working. Do not block the real job on the post.
- Healthy recurring jobs and scheduled routines stay off the board. Do not clutter it with daily or hourly runs that are going fine. If a recurring job becomes `blocked` (it needs human input or approval) or `failed`, push it so it surfaces in Needs attention. Once it is fixed or unblocked, push `done` so it clears out of Needs attention. Use `blocked` only when you actually asked a human.

## CLI

- `statuspan agent` prints the skill that ships in the binary. `statuspan agent prompt` prints a short snippet for AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. `statuspan agent json` prints a discovery document. `statuspan agent install` writes the skill into agent directories (`--target auto|agents|claude|cursor|codex|all`, `--dir`, `--home`, `--dry-run`).
- `statuspan run --agent NAME --job ID [--title T] [--recurring] -- COMMAND` posts `running`, heartbeats, then `done` or `failed`, and exits with the command's status. `--recurring` posts nothing on success and one `failed` on a non-zero exit. A command that cannot start is exit 127 and one `failed` post.
- `statuspan hooks install <tool>` reports a Claude Code (`claude`), Grok (`grok`), Codex (`codex`), or Cursor (`cursor`) session from lifecycle hooks (prompt, tool calls, permission prompts, turn end, session end). `--project`, `--dry-run`, and `statuspan hooks uninstall <tool>` are available. Claude and Grok print nothing back into the session. Codex prints `{}` on stdout so it is not added as developer context. Cursor prints `{"continue":true}` for beforeSubmitPrompt and `{}` for every other event, and it does not register permission hooks. The hook does not block. Secrets in titles and notes are redacted best-effort. Stop runs every turn, so an idle interactive session shows done until the next prompt. Grok project hooks need folder trust (`/hooks-trust` or `--trust`). Codex hooks need to be trusted in `/hooks` (trust is per hook hash). Codex project hooks load only in trusted projects. `CODEX_HOME` selects the Codex home when `--home` is not set. Grok also reads Claude and Cursor hook files and reports those sessions as Grok. The Cursor IDE agent and the Cursor CLI both read `hooks.json`, and Cursor reloads that file automatically.
- `STATUSPAN_AGENT` is the default for `run --agent`. `STATUSPAN_URL` is the full local jobs endpoint for `post` and `run` (for example `http://127.0.0.1:14477/api/jobs`). `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE` is a file containing the relay write token, used when `STATUSPAN_TOKEN` is unset.
- The same recurring rule applies to the CLI: healthy routines stay off the board. Push `blocked` or `failed` when a routine needs a person or has failed, then push `done` once it is resolved.

## Connect another machine to your relay

Use this when a second computer, a cloud agent, or CI should post to the same board. Those agents cannot reach `127.0.0.1` on the machine that runs the board.

Token roles:

| Token | Role |
| --- | --- |
| write | Per machine or agent. Post only. Cannot read the board. |
| read | Local daemon and board only. Cannot post. |
| admin | Mint and revoke tokens, create workspaces. Never give it to bots. |

1. On the machine that has the admin token, from `relay/`:

```bash
export RELAY_URL="https://<your-relay>.workers.dev"
export ADMIN_TOKEN=$(cat admin-token)
node scripts/admin.mjs mint <workspace> --kind write --agent <agent-name> --label <machine-label> --out write-token
```

The command is `node scripts/admin.mjs mint <workspace> --kind read|write [--agent <name>] [--label <label>] [--out <path>]`. A write token requires `--agent`. `--label` is optional and should name the machine. `--out` writes only the token (mode 0600) and prints `saved to <path>`. The token is scoped to that agent name; posts from the new machine must use the same `--agent`. `RELAY_URL` and `ADMIN_TOKEN` come from the environment, or `--relay-url` / `--admin-token-file`.

2. On the new machine, save the token to `~/.config/statuspan/token` (`chmod 600`). Never put the token in shell history or chat. Prefer copying the file minted with `--out`, or pasting it into an editor. Do not `echo` the token on the command line.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/statuspan
# copy write-token onto the new machine as ~/.config/statuspan/token
chmod 600 ~/.config/statuspan/token
```

3. On the new machine, set these and persist them in your shell rc (`~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`):

```bash
export STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL="https://<your-relay>.workers.dev"
export STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE="<workspace>"
export STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE="$HOME/.config/statuspan/token"
```

4. Verify. Post a test job (the agent name must match the token) and check the local board within a few seconds:

```bash
statuspan post --agent "<agent-name>" --job connect-test --state running --note "from the new machine"
```

Then look for that job on the board, or `curl -s "http://${STATUSPAN_ADDR:-127.0.0.1:4477}/api/jobs"`.

## Where did this update come from?

A hostname in a note is self-reported. The agent typed it, and a client can fake it.

The relay stamps each accepted write with the write token's label (or the token id when the label is empty), the request IP, the country, and the time it received the update. Clients cannot set or overwrite `via`, `ip`, `country`, or `received_at`. The board shows a muted line such as `via ci-builder · 203.0.113.10 · US`. A post that never went through the relay shows `via local`.

The local board only shows this after it is running a daemon build that understands the new fields. An older daemon still syncs jobs; it just will not display the stamp.

## Self-host the relay

Cloud and remote agents (Cursor cloud agents, CI, other servers) cannot reach `127.0.0.1` on your machine. They post to a relay with a write token stored as a secret. The local daemon pulls those jobs in. If you do not want to run Cloudflare yourself, use Hosted Relay: https://statuspan.com/cloud.

A free Cloudflare account and Node.js are enough. From `relay/`:

```bash
cd relay
npm install
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler deploy
openssl rand -hex 32 > admin-token
npx wrangler secret put ADMIN_TOKEN < admin-token
chmod 600 admin-token
export RELAY_URL=https://statuspan-relay.<account>.workers.dev
export ADMIN_TOKEN=$(cat admin-token)
node scripts/admin.mjs create-workspace home
node scripts/admin.mjs mint home --kind write --agent MyBot --label laptop --out write-token
node scripts/admin.mjs mint home --kind read --label board --out read-token
chmod 600 write-token read-token
```

`wrangler deploy` prints the `workers.dev` URL. Never commit `admin-token`. A write token posts for one agent and cannot read the board. A read token feeds the board and cannot post. The admin token creates workspaces and mints, lists, and revokes tokens. Never give it to bots.

Point the daemon at the relay with `relay.json` in the data directory (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/statuspan/relay.json`):

```json
{"url":"https://statuspan-relay.<account>.workers.dev","workspace":"home","read_token":"<paste the read token>"}
```

`chmod 600` that file and restart the daemon. It polls about every 3 seconds. Alternative env: `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL`, `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE`, and `STATUSPAN_RELAY_READ_TOKEN`.

Agents post with `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL`, `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE`, and `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE` (or `STATUSPAN_TOKEN` as a secret), then `statuspan post` or `statuspan run`, or curl with `Authorization: Bearer`.

Full steps: https://statuspan.com/relay and https://statuspan.com/llms-full.txt.

## Specs

- [Full reference](https://statuspan.com/llms-full.txt): CLI, HTTP API, relay, and copy-paste clients
- [Self-host the relay](https://statuspan.com/relay): Cloudflare Worker setup, tokens, and `relay.json`
- [Hosted Relay](https://statuspan.com/cloud): no-setup relay, waitlist
- [Agent skill](https://statuspan.com/skill.md): drop-in instructions for a coding agent
- [OpenAPI](https://statuspan.com/openapi.json): local daemon and self-hosted relay
- [Job update schema](https://statuspan.com/schema/job-update.schema.json): JSON Schema for one update or a batch
- [Mac app](https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest/download/StatusPan.dmg): StatusPan.dmg, universal, macOS 12 or later
- [Installer](https://statuspan.com/install.sh): macOS and Linux, no sudo, installs to `~/.local/bin/statuspan`
- [Releases](https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest): CLI binaries and StatusPan.dmg
- [Source](https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan): MIT
